sentences.text:
This Civil Miscellaneous Appeal has been filed, by the claimant, challenging the quantum of compensation, awarded by the judgement and decree, dated, 06.10.2016, made in MCOP.No.2106 of 2014, by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (Additional District Judge cum Special Judge for EC Act)
2.
On 24.08.2014 at about 11 a.m., one Mr.Pichaipillai was riding his Honda Activa two wheeler along with one Mr.Veerappan on the extreme left side of the Namakkal to Karur NH Road.
While going near Raj Bhavan Hotel near Pulavarpalayam Tollgate, a lorry bearing Regn.No.TN-48/K- 7267 came in a rash and negligent manner and hit against the motor cyclist.

Due to the impact,
Pichaipllai sustained fatal injuries and died on the way to hospital.

Since the accident had occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the lorry, they filed a claim petition against the owner of the offending vehicle/1st respondent and insurer of the vehicle/2nd respondent Insurance Company, the claimants/legal heirs of the deceased 2 of 12 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis have filed a claim petition before the Tribunal, seeking a compensation of Rs.75,00,000/- on various heads, for the death of the deceased against the 1st and 2nd respondents.
The claim petition was resisted on various grounds, by the 2nd Respondent/ Insurance Company, by filing a counter.
3. On the side of the claimants, PW.1 to PW5 were examined and Ex.P1 to Ex.P13 were marked.
On the side of respondents, Ex.R.1 was marked.
Ex.C1-summons to District Education Officer was also marked.

4. Finding that the accident had occurred only due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle belonged to the 1st Respondent and insured with the 2nd Respondent, the Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.29,14,720/-, to be paid by the respondents jointly and severally to the claimants 1 to 4 under various heads, with interest at 7.5% p.a. from the date of the claim petition till the date of realization, to be paid by the 2nd Respondent Insurance Company,
as detailed below:-

 claimant

3 Loss of love and affection Rs. 40,000/-
 (Rs.10,000 x 4)
 4

. Funeral Expenses Rs. 10,000/-
 Total Rs.29,14,720/-

sentences.text: Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the tribunal, this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal has been filed by the claimants.
6. This Court heard the learned counsel for the Appellants and the 2nd Respondent Insurance Company, considered their submissions and also perused the entire materials placed on record.

7. The learned counsel appearing for the appellants submitted that at the time of accident, the deceased was employed as Head Master in Govt. School Valikandapuram and was earning Rs.79,415/- and he got retired from service on 30.06.2014 and after his superannuation, his service was extended till the next academic year i.e., from 01.7.2014 to 30.05.2015, 4 of 12 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis whereas the accident occurred on 24.08.2014 and if he is alive, the deceased would have earned his salary for the extended period of his service from 01.07.2014 to 30.05.2015.

Whereas, the tribunal, without taking into account the salary of the extended period of his service from 24.08.2014 to 30.05.2015, arrived at a conclusion by taking 50% of the last drawn salary of Rs.39,510/- being Rs.79,020/- as his pension and applied multiplier of 9, awarded compensation towards total loss of income at Rs.28,44,720/-.
8.

It is his further submission that as per Ex.P.12 Salary certificate of deceased Pitchai Pillai, the deceased received Rs.1,03,1098/- for the period from 1.7.2014 to 24.08.2014 and it is deposed by PW3-Superintendent in chief Educational office that a monthly salary of Rs.76,131 would be given to the deceased for his service extension period.
But without considering the above evidence, the tribunal has erroneously fixed the monthly income of the deceased only at Rs.39,510/-.

As per Sarla Verma's case, when more than 3 persons are claimants, 1/4th income has to be deducted towards personal expenses, but the tribunal has deducted 1/3rd of the income of the deceased towards his personal expenses.
Further, the 5 of 12 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis tribunal has not awarded 15% of the income towards furture prospects while awarding compensation as per law laid down in Pranay Sethy's Case.

The tribunal has also awarded very meagre amount under the heads loss of consortium, love and affection, funeral expenses and not awarded anything towards transport,
damages and loss of estate.
Therefore he prayed for allowing the appeal.

9. Per contra, the learned counsel appearing for the 2nd respondent /Insurance Company submitted that while the driver of the lorry rode the vehicle slowly and cautiously, the appellant rode his motor vehicle in a negligent manner and dashed against the 1st respondent lorry, thereby, he invited the accident on 24.08.2014.
The deceased got retired from service on 30.06.2014 and the tribunal taking into consideration 50% of his last drawn salary of Rs.79,020/-, rightly calculated his pension amount at Rs.39,510/-.

Considering the age of the deceased at the time of the accident and applying correct multiplier of 9 and after deducting 1/3 towards his personal expenses, it awarded compensation of Rs.28,44,720/- which is perfectly in order and the same cannot be interfered with.
He further 6 of 12 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis submitted that in respect of other heads, the amounts awarded by the tribunal is correct and reasonable.
Therefore, he prayed for dismissal of this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal.

10. Since there is no quarrel over the manner, in which the accident had occurred, negligence aspect and the liability aspect as well and the dispute is only with regard to the quantum of compensation,

sentences.text: the findings of the Tribunal with respect to the manner of the accident, negligence aspect and liability aspect are confirmed and also it is not necessary to narrate the entire facts in detail in respect of the accident.
11. Admittedly, the accident was happened on 24.08.2014, whereas deceased retired as Head Master from his service on 30.06.2014.

As per Ex.P.12 salary certificate of deceased, the deceased has received Rs.1,03,198/- for the period from 1.7.2014 to 24.08.2014 and as per the evidence of PW3, a monthly salary of Rs.76,131 will be given to the deceased for extension of his service period.

In view of the above, the deceased is entitled for claiming compensation of Rs.39510/- from 7 of 12 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 24.08.2014 to 30.05.2015 for a period of 9 months apart from the pension amount of Rs.39,510/- granted towards loss of income by applying 9 multiplier.
12.
It is also seen that the tribunal has not awarded any amount under the head future prospects while awarding compensation as per Pranay Sethy's Case.

Hence, a sum of Rs.4,26,708/- is being awarded under the head loss of future prospects (15% of 28,44,720)
13.
The amount awarded under the head loss of love and affection is found to be very low, hence it is enhanced to Rs.40,000/- from Rs.10,000/- (Rs.4 x 40,000 = 1,60,000/-).
Apart from the above, the amount awarded under the other heads by the tribunal is very very meagre.
Therefore, towards funeral expenses a sum of Rs.15,000/- is awarded instead of Rs.10,000/-.
Since already an amount of Rs.40,000/- was awarded towards love and affection to each claimant, the amount awarded under the head 'loss of consortium' is hereby deleted.
In addition to that, this Court awards Rs.15,000/- towards loss of Estate.
Thus, this court awards the enhanced 8 of 12 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis compensation as follows:
Conventional
Heads High Court

Loss of Income 28,44,720  Adding 15% towards loss of income 4,26,708 Loss of income during extension of 3,55,590 service period (9 x 39510) Loss of love and affection 1,60,000 4 x 40,000 Funeral expenses 15000 Loss of estate 15000

In all, the total compensation is redetermined at Rs.38,17,018/- which shall carry interest @
7.5% p.a. from the date of the claim petition till the date of realisation.
15.In fine, this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is partly allowed.

In all, the claimants are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.38,17,018/-, (Rupees thirty eight lakhs seventeen thousand and eighteen only) with interest @ 7.5% p.a. from the date of the claim petition till the date of realisation, as redetermined below:-

claimants shall pay the proper court fee for the enhanced compensation amount.

The 2nd Respondent / Insurance Company is directed to deposit the entire award amount with interest at 7.5% p.a. from the date of the claim petition till the date of deposit, after deducting the amount, if any, already deposited and also the interest for the delay in filing the appeal, if any for the enhanced compensation,
within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.

On such deposit 10 of 12 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis being made, the Tribunal is directed to transfer, by way of RTGS, the entire compensation amount, with interest due, directly to the bank account of the claimants as per the apportionment made by the tribunal, within a period of three weeks thereafter.
No costs.
